output_json.patch_notes: In StaticHandlerImpl.handle(), inserted `.replace('\\', '/')` on the fully-decoded request path immediately before the second HttpUtils.removeDots() call, so backslash-delimited dot segments (literal '\' or decoded '%5C') are collapsed by the same '../' removal logic that already protects forward-slash paths. Added two regression tests to the existing StaticHandlerTest suite (testBackslashTraversalCannotEscapeWebRoot, testEncodedBackslashTraversalCannotEscapeWebRoot) asserting that requests using backslash (raw or percent-encoded) to reach a resource one level above the configured webroot classpath root (favicon.ico, a sibling of the 'webroot' test resource dir) return 404 rather than being served. Ran the full StaticHandlerTest suite (65 tests) before and after the fix: all pass with the fix; also confirmed via `mvn -B -DskipTests package` that the module builds cleanly.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only affects how the request path string is normalized before it's used to locate files under webRoot; forward-slash-only paths (the overwhelmingly common case) are completely unaffected since '\'->'/' replacement is a no-op for them. Because the actual filesystem escape only manifests on Windows (where '\' is a real path separator), the added regression tests pass identically before and after the fix when run on Linux CI/containers — they lock in the intended sanitization contract and will catch a regression on Windows, mirroring the approach the upstream Vert.x project itself used for the analogous CVE-2023-24815 fix (their StaticHandlerWindowsTest). No behavior change for legitimate paths containing literal backslashes as ordinary (non-separator) filename characters on POSIX systems was intentionally introduced beyond what's needed to close the traversal bypass, since such filenames are already unusual/unsupported through URL paths.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-022 path traversal in vertx-web's StaticHandlerImpl: the decoded request path was dot-segment-normalized via HttpUtils.removeDots(), which only recognizes '/' as a path separator. A raw or percent-encoded backslash ('\' / '%5C') therefore survived normalization untouched and, once concatenated with webRoot and resolved by a backslash-aware filesystem (Windows), could walk outside the configured web root (CVE-2023-24815-class bug). The fix canonicalizes backslashes to forward slashes before dot-segment removal so the existing '../' collapsing logic uniformly neutralizes both slash- and backslash-based traversal sequences, regardless of the host OS's separator convention. This is a single choke-point fix in StaticHandlerImpl.handle() that covers every downstream use of the computed `path` (getFile/pathOffset, cache key, hidden-file check, directory listing, etc.), so all traces in the alert (which all flow through this same `path` variable) are addressed by one change.
